messages.subject: Seqz data vs binned seqz data
messages.subject_clean: Seqz data vs binned seqz data
messages.body_plain:
I have been attempting to run a successful sequenza workflow on my data and have run into a few issues and questions.

seqz.data <- read.seqz("sample_data/Brca1Br10-T/Brca1Br10-T.seqz.gz")
Error in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines, na.strings, : scan() expected 'an integer', got 'position'

My seqz data was created chr by chr and then zcat merged. Initially I had generated some seqz files using the entire sample data and that was properly read by seqz.read, but then I adopted a chr by chr method to make things go faster, and now I am halted. I am however, able to read in binned data from sequenza-utils.py seqz-binning -w 50. Something is clearly different in the files, I am just not sure what I need to be looking for to debug it.

Thank you.

messages.body_plain:
I do not fully understand this methods pipeline but I was curios why in the example sequenza.extract is executed on the raw seqz data data.file, instead of the GC normalized data in the seqz.data variable (according to the usage example)

test <- sequenza.extract(data.file)

I had actually tried to run sequenza.extract on seqz.data but receive an error:

> test <- sequenza.extract(seqz.data) Error in pipe(paste("gzip -d -c", file, "| cut -f 1,6,10")) : invalid 'description' argument

Can anyone explain this to me in a bit further detail? Is there just something wrong with my data files or am I just making a poor assumption on what sequenza is actually doing? If sequenza.extract(data.file) is correct for real data then what purpose does the GC normalization steps serve?

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: incomplete seqz file generated
messages.body_plain:
Hi Igor,

Thanks for using Sequenza!
You should check the GC file, and the fasta file you used to generate it: the order of the chromosome should be similar in all 3 files.
I bet this is the problem: some reference are ordered by chromosome size, so chrX is right after chr7.
The script skipped all the other chromosomes to reach chrX, and after processing it there was nothing left to process in the pileup (well there should be chrY...).
To verify this you could look at the output of something like:

zcat hg19_gc50.txt.gz | grep variableStep | uniq

I'm sorry about that, I kept the script really simple so it can't figure out shuffled-chromosomes files.
A universal solution for this problem is to process the bam/pileups chromosome by chromosome, and then merge or perform other operations on the files afterwards. It's also considerably faster (~1h per exome).

There is an example in the wiki on how to use the "wrapper":
https://bitbucket.org/ffavero/sequenza/wiki/Sequenza_Utils#markdown-header-wrapper-to-parallelize-standardize-execution

Best

Francesco

messages.subject: Error in contour.default
messages.body_plain:
I tried running the R part of Sequenza and just trying to replicate the most basic example:
sequenza_extract = sequenza.extract("sample.seqz.gz")
sequenza_fit = sequenza.fit(sequenza_extract)
sequenza.results(sequenza.extract = sequenza_extract, cp.table = sequenza_fit, sample.id = "sample", out.dir="sequenza_results")

Unfortunately, I get an error:
> sequenza.results(sequenza.extract = sequenza_extract, cp.table = sequenza_fit, sample.id = "sample", out.dir="sequenza_results")
Error in contour.default(x = cp.table$ploidy, y = cp.table$cellularity,  :
  invalid NA contour values

Am I doing something wrong?

messages.subject: Re: Error in contour.default
messages.body_plain:
H Igor,
This problem could occur when one or more segment is really small and produce an NA.
As a easy fix, you can try to use the newer version of the package.
In my opinion is a much better version., there are tons of fixes, and both the model and the segmentation have improved.
You can even use segmentation results from external tools (If you already have the segment called with other software)
Your can install it directly with devtools:

library(devtools)

install_bitbucket(repo = "sequenza", username = "ffavero", ref = "dnorm")

Hopefully this would fix your problem, otherwise you can send me the segmentation from the sequenza.extract object, and I'll try to fix the behaviour of the function.

(I've tested extensively but I might not ahave experienced all the possible problems).

Thanks

Francesco

messages.subject: Re: Error in contour.default
messages.body_plain:
Hi Igor,

With your data I would try to use different segmentation parameters; for instance in the sequneza.extract command I would try the argument breaks.method = "full".
This uses two segmentations merging the default on heterozygous positions as well a "classical" segmentation on the depth ratio only.
It might lead to smaller segments, but you will gain in precision.

I'm curious, is this targeted re-sequencing? single cell sequencing?

If it's targeted sequencing at hight depth (~500X or 1000X), and you have validated mutations, you could use a different model which included in the package. We didn't test it too much - due to lack of data, mainly-.

You can try in the sequenza.fit the argument method = "mufreq". This would use the mutations frequency instead the segmentations results.

I'm sorry for the vague support I'm giving you here, but the technology you are using have some practical things impeding the full use of the package.
(Of course we should be able to work around it though)

Francesco
